anchors.name: ISO/IEC 42001
anchors.binding: International standard; certifiable by a certification body
anchors.asks: A management system for AI: set roles, assess each AI system's risks and impact, apply controls across the AI life cycle, then monitor and keep improving.
anchors.evidence: Test reports and a record of each system's risks, tests and changes that your management system can use.

anchors.name: ISO/IEC 23894
anchors.binding: International standard giving guidance; not certifiable
anchors.asks: Apply ISO 31000 risk management to AI, so an existing risk register can take in AI risks.
anchors.evidence: The risks each evaluation finds, written so they can go into your existing risk register.

anchors.name: ISO/IEC 42005
anchors.asks: How and when to assess an AI system's impact on people and society, and how to document it.
anchors.evidence: Test results and failure lists that an impact assessment can cite.

anchors.name: NIST AI RMF and the GenAI Profile
anchors.issuer: US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
anchors.binding: Voluntary framework, with a voluntary profile for generative AI
anchors.asks: Govern, map, measure and manage AI risks across the life cycle; the Generative AI Profile names risks such as confabulation and over-reliance on AI output.
anchors.evidence: Measured test results on your own questions, re-run when the model changes, with every failure listed.

anchors.name: NIST AI 600-1, Generative AI Profile
anchors.issuer: US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
anchors.asks: Names 12 generative AI risks, including confabulation, human-AI configuration, data privacy, information security and value chain integration.
anchors.evidence: Test results that count confabulated answers and show where a person must check the output.

anchors.name: OECD AI Principles
anchors.asks: Traceability of datasets, processes and decisions, and ongoing risk management across the AI system life cycle.
anchors.evidence: Answers and test records that show which source, model version and setting produced each result.

anchors.name: EU AI Act: reaches AI output used in the EU
anchors.binding: EU law; it reaches providers and deployers outside the EU when their AI output is used in the EU
anchors.asks: Measures to support staff AI literacy, telling people when they deal with AI, and human oversight, monitoring and logs for high-risk AI. Annex III high-risk duties apply from 2 December 2027 (as amended in July 2026), and new prohibitions from 2 December 2026.
anchors.evidence: Test reports, oversight and log records, and staff briefing material that your own AI Act duties can draw on.

anchors.name: GDPR Art 22: people, not just software, decide
anchors.binding: EU law; it reaches organisations outside the EU that offer services to, or monitor, people in the EU
anchors.asks: No decision based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects on a person, unless the law allows it and safeguards apply: human intervention, a chance to give a view and a right to contest.
anchors.evidence: A workflow where a named person approves every draft before it is sent or acted on, with each approval logged.
